title: Fireworks AI Pricing: Models, GPUs & Billing (2026)
summary: Fireworks AI pricing charges per token consumed plus GPU time for dedicated capacity. Your costs increase only with resources you actually use.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


Does Fireworks AI have a free tier? Treat it as a trial at most, not a place to run production.


The metered unit is the token, so any free allowance is a small credit that gets used up quickly. Check the pricing page at signup for what your account receives, and don't build a cost plan around it.


### How do Fireworks AI credits work and do they expire?


Because credits are a prepaid balance that metered usage draws down, they lower your invoice but don't change the per-token price. Whether a given credit expires depends on how it was issued, since promotional credits and purchased balances are often treated differently.


Read the terms shown beside the credit in your billing page. If a balance has an expiry date, you can only use it on serverless token usage before that date, and it won't cover a dedicated GPU left running past it.


### Can I set a spending limit on Fireworks AI?


Look in your account billing settings first, because that's where any account-level cap or alert would live, and use it if your account offers one.


Whatever the dashboard offers, you have two controls of your own. Set a maximum output length on every request, since output tokens are the expensive side of the bill.


And treat each dedicated deployment as a meter that runs until you shut it down, so delete it when the test is over.


### Is Fireworks AI cheaper than OpenAI for open models?


Only compare like with like: the same open-weight model, the same input and output rates, and the same traffic. OpenAI's flagship models aren't open-weight models, so a price comparison against GPT-6 Astra or GPT-6.1 Sol is really a comparison of two different products.


When an open model is good enough for your task, Fireworks AI wins, because you then pay that model's per-token rate instead of a frontier rate.


If a closed model needs fewer retries or shorter outputs, its higher unit price can still produce the lower bill.


### What happens when I hit a Fireworks AI rate limit?


Rejected rather than queued, your request usually comes back as an HTTP 429 error. Handle it by retrying with a growing delay and a retry cap, so a burst doesn't turn into a storm of repeat calls.


If you hit the limit constantly, that's the signal to look at the limits attached to your account, or to move steady, predictable volume to a dedicated deployment and price it against the cheaper GPU clouds first.
